The Rest is Confetti

Creator Mike Flanagan wrote the monologue during a period of personal exhaustion and reflection on loss, as detailed in essays like Stuck in Act Two. Flanagan detailed this exact creative mindset in personal essays published on his Tumblr blog, noting that the monologue was written late at night during a grueling, isolating 100-day shoot. He channeled his deep grief, his reflections on losing two loved ones to suicide, and the guilt of using his family's real experiences as "building material" for the show directly into Nell's final words. The resulting line ("The rest is confetti") was meant to signify that despite life's chaotic, non-linear trauma, unconditional love and forgiveness are the only truths that endure.
